source_inventory_policy: Normal coverage is source-first and contains exactly the two visibly displayed Definitions on printed page 10, the Section 3 prose definition of marriage instability, and Theorems 1 and 2. Source presentation and exact byte-pinned spans determine this inventory; map keys and Lean declaration names do not. The exact Section 4 top-q waiting-list procedure is retained as a semantic atom of Theorem 2 because that theorem names the procedure's assignment.
source_kind_policy: Normal named-theory scope contains source-presented theoretical definitions, theorems, lemmas, and corollaries. Examples, proof-local notation, proof steps, runtime remarks, and unnumbered extensions are deep-audit material unless the user requests a deep all-prose review. A named result may retain procedure semantics as an atom when its statement explicitly refers to the output of that procedure.
declared_scope_exclusions: Examples 1-3, ranking matrices, numerical iterations, and the roommate nonexistence example are outside normal named-theory coverage; Example 3's embedded roommate-stability definition is retained in the prose-definition ledger as user-approved deep-only material.

Theorem 1 proof steps, its n-squared-minus-2n-plus-2 stage remark, unequal-side extensions, and symmetric proposer observations are proof or deep-audit material rather than independent normal-scope named results.
Theorem 2 proof-local possible-college notation and the unnumbered inverted college-proposing observation are outside normal named-theory coverage.

source_named_result_inventory_review.method: Independently indexed the exact current primary-scan extraction before consulting source-map keys or Lean names. The source-only extractor finds two unnumbered displayed Definitions and Theorems 1 and 2; the named-result receipt digest contains Theorems 1 and 2 after the separate prose-definition inventory claims the displayed definitions. That complete prose-definition pass adds the Section 3 marriage-instability definition, records the Example 3 roommate definition as deep-only under the standing user scope instruction, and records possible-college as proof-local notation.

theorem2_applicant_optimality.statement: Theorem 2: the Section 4 arbitrary-quota applicant-proposing waiting-list procedure returns a completed-standard stable assignment under which every applicant is at least as well off as under every other completed-standard stable assignment.
theorem2_applicant_optimality.source_location: source.txt:232-249; source.txt:253-255 (printed pages 13-14, Sections 4-5 and Theorem 2)
theorem2_applicant_optimality.source_note: The procedure filters applications by the source's pairwise mutual eligibility convention, then each college retains exactly its top q among its prior waiting list and new applicants. No extra global applicant-positive-implies-college-positive premise is part of the theorem. Under the documented completed-stability reading of Sections 4--5, the comparison class is quota-feasible and individually rational and has no mutually acceptable block through a vacancy or replacement of a current assignee. The literal page-10 replacement-pair definition remains separately formalized rather than silently strengthened.
